intro: Timor-Leste, or East Timor, became the first new country of the 21st century in 2002, after centuries of Portuguese rule and a long struggle against Indonesian occupation.

chapters.title: Sandalwood island
text: Timor was famous for sandalwood, traded with China and Java for centuries. Local kingdoms ruled the island.

chapters.title: Portuguese Timor
text: Portugal arrived in the 1500s and ruled the eastern half, while the Dutch took the west, which became part of Indonesia. Catholicism spread under Portuguese rule.
During World War Two, Australian soldiers fought the Japanese here with help from Timorese people, tens of thousands of whom died.

chapters.title: Occupation and independence
text: Portugal left in 1975, and nine days after independence was declared, Indonesia invaded. Under Indonesian occupation, over 100,000 people died from violence, hunger and disease.

In 1999 Timorese voted overwhelmingly for independence in a UN referendum. Militias destroyed much of the country before international peacekeepers arrived. Timor-Leste became independent on 20 May 2002, and in 2025 it joined ASEAN.

highlight.title: Nobel Prize
highlight.text: José Ramos-Horta and Bishop Carlos Belo shared the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize.

keyTerms.meaning: A public vote on a single question.
International troops sent to keep peace.
